newsitem.title: USA: Latin American debt prices sink on Brazil worries.
newsitem.headline: Latin American debt prices sink on Brazil worries.

text.p: Latin American bond prices sank Tuesday amid concerns that recent currency turmoil in Asia might destabilize Brazil's economy.
Fears that Brazil might be forced to devalue rocked financial markets across the region, even though Brazilian officials vowed to maintain the country's exchange rate policy.
"There is a psychological snowball that is taking place, because nothing fundamental happened to Brazil today," said Larry Krohn, Latin American economist at UBS Securities.

Stock markets across latin America took a severe beating Tuesday, as the Bovespa index .BVSP ended 8.51 percent lower, the biggest one-day drop since january 1995. Mexico's IPC index fell 1.73 percent, and Argentina's MerVal sank 3.37 percent.
But U.S. analysts were quick to draw distinctions between conditions in Brazil than Thailand, where a massive current account defict forced a de facto devaluation.

Brazil's current account deficit widened to 4.2 percent of GDP, but U.S. economists defended the country's stability and characterized the sharp price drops as painful corrective medicine for the strong rally over recent weeks.

Michael Cembalest, head quantitative strategist at JP Morgan, said the broad nature of the selling indicated that the plunge had more to do with overall price inflation than fears of Brazilian policy.
"There had been a lot of unbridled optimism in the market and once you see a couple of signs of weakness there is a collective mentality that it's time to take profits," Cembalest said.

Brady bond traders reported heavy flows as U.S. institutions unloaded the paper accumulated over the market's recent spectacular rally. Much of the momentum came from local Brazilian accounts, traders said.
"On the dealer side there is a lot of changing hands," said Marcelo Fleury, vice president at broker/dealer Garband Corp. "It's a good excuse to take profits out of this market."
Most Brady bonds widened 20-30 basis points against comparable U.S. Treasuries.
The liquid Brazilian "C" bond sank to 80-7/8 bid, and the country's global bond due 2027 dropped to 96-3/4. Argentine FRBs slipped to 93-3/4, while Mexico's global bond due 2026 fell to 115-3/8.
Traders were reluctant to forecast an immediate end to the bleeding.
"If you believe this is a correction, there's more room for correction," one Brady trader said.
